source_name: DevelopmentAid organisation profile — Asseco Macedonia
why_relevant: Aggregator profile confirming Asseco's registered MK entity and its donor-project footprint; useful for linking a global vendor brand to its local legal entity, which is the name that appears in MK registries and contracts.

source_name: Vrabotuvanje.com.mk — job board (Economics/Finance/Accounting category)
why_relevant: Main MK job portal; carries bank postings such as Капитал Банка 'Соработник во сектор за контрола и усогласеност', НЛБ 'Сегмент за спречување перење пари', ProCredit AML/CFT specialist. Volume and titles of such ads is the leading indicator of a mandate being internalised.

source_name: Kariera.mk — job board (search interface)
why_relevant: Second major MK job board; hosts National Bank vacancy notices and commercial-bank compliance/reporting roles. Complements vrabotuvanje.com.mk — some employers post exclusively on one.

source_name: НБРСМ — Вработување во Народната банка (NBRSM careers)
why_relevant: The supervisor's own hiring is the purest indirect signal: postings for 'супервизор II степен' in Дирекција за супервизија на далечина и лиценцирање or Дирекција за теренска супервизија reveal where NBRSM is expanding supervisory capacity (e.g. licensing of PSPs/EMIs, on-site AML inspection) months before new rulebooks or inspection cycles appear.

source_name: University career/announcement boards republishing NBRSM vacancies (UKIM Economics Faculty, UACS, UIST)
why_relevant: MK faculties republish the full text of NBRSM and bank vacancy notices, often persisting after the original notice is taken down from nbrm.mk. Useful as a mirror/archive layer for dating supervisory hiring waves.

source_name: Македонска банкарска асоцијација (МБА) — announcements, working groups, member trainings
why_relevant: The banking association coordinates sector-wide implementation and publishes joint statements dated to regulatory go-lives (e.g. its notice that Strong Customer Authentication under the Law on Payment Services becomes mandatory from 1 March 2026). Its tag pages (Народна банка, КИБС) act as a pointer map of who is preparing what; association seminars named after draft rules are the classic early-warning artefact for this cell.

source_name: АБИТ — Академија за банкарство и информатичка технологија (seminars)
why_relevant: Dedicated MK banking academy (est. 2014, >100 specialist seminars) whose seminar catalogue is titled after live regulatory topics — a seminar named after a draft rulebook dates the sector's implementation window. Seminar agendas also name the lecturers (often NBRSM/bank staff), yielding an actor map.

source_name: Стопанска комора на Северна Македонија — Финансии section & seminar programme
why_relevant: The Chamber runs paid seminars for corporates and financial institutions on new laws and hosts a 'прописи/info' regulatory section; a chamber seminar announced on a draft law is a dated signal that the business side is preparing. Also carries consultation invitations to members.

source_name: МАСИТ — Стопанска комора за информатички и комуникациски технологии (specialised payments/SEPA events)
why_relevant: ICT chamber that co-organises technical workshops with KIBS on payment-standard migrations (e.g. a specialised SEPA-transfers workshop, 19 Nov 2025, on national capacity and the path to integration). Such vendor/IT-facing agendas date technical implementation windows for SEPA/ISO 20022 well ahead of regulatory deadlines.

source_name: КИБС АД Скопје — Клириншка куќа (events, licences, member communications)
why_relevant: National clearing house; hosted the EACHA annual conference in Skopje and obtained an NBRSM licence for an instant credit transfer payment system (reported 17.9.2025). Its event hosting, licence milestones and member workshops mark the operational timetable that banks must align to.

source_name: Finelevate Digital Summit (Skopje, 16 Sept 2026) — conference agenda
why_relevant: Business conference on the future of digital finance for the banking, insurance and fintech sectors in Skopje; announced topics explicitly include regulatory compliance (регулаторна усогласеност), payment innovation, digital identity, cyber security and data modernisation. Its agenda and speaker roster is a direct read on which mandates institutions are staffing for in 2026-27.

source_name: MicroBalkans (Skopje) — regional non-bank finance conference
why_relevant: Third edition brings 200+ financial-sector representatives from 15 European countries to Skopje, explicitly including non-bank financial institutions, microcredit institutions, savings houses, fintechs and REGULATORS. Panel titles reveal the regulatory agenda facing MK non-bank PSPs/lenders; the delegate mix is an actor map for the sector.

source_name: Управа за финансиско разузнавање (УФР / Financial Intelligence Unit) — trainings, guidance, annual reports
why_relevant: Statutory duty to train authorised AML/CFT officers in obliged entities; publishes guidance (упатства) and training records for the banking sector (e.g. on implementing international restrictive measures). Announcement of a training programme on a new obligation dates the compliance implementation window; annual reports enumerate how many bank officers were trained on what.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — Семинари и обуки
why_relevant: Ministry-run seminar/training listing; MoF is the sponsor of AML and financial-sector legislation, so a training titled after a draft law signals the drafting stage has reached implementation planning.

source_name: ИОРРСМ — Институт на овластени ревизори на РСМ (CPD/КПУ annual training programme)
why_relevant: The auditors' institute publishes a yearly continuing-professional-development (КПУ) programme listing seminar titles and hours — observed to include topics such as the Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems and the role of the FIU. A regulated profession's mandatory CPD catalogue is a dated, structured index of which rules the market must absorb this year.

source_name: Агенција за супервизија на осигурување (АСО) — training/manuals and licensing exams
why_relevant: Insurance supervisor publishes examination manuals and certification/training material for agents and brokers (e.g. Прирачник за застапници). Changes to the certification syllabus track changes in the regulatory regime; relevant where the run scope covers 'both' sectors and bancassurance distribution.

source_name: Bank career/press pages — Комерцијална банка, Стопанска банка, НЛБ, ТТК, УНИБанка, ПроКредит, Силк Роуд, Капитал
why_relevant: Primary issuers of the hiring and award signals: bank career pages carry the full job description (naming internal units and reporting obligations), and press pages carry award/certification announcements (e.g. Комерцијална банка named Best Bank in Macedonia 2026 by Global Finance, 15th time) and regulatory-readiness notices (Стопанска банка's customer information pages on the Law on Payment Services). Bank-side notices to customers about a law are a dated proxy for the go-live of that law.

source_name: LinkedIn — MK bank/PSP company pages and job postings (compliance, regulatory reporting, AML)
why_relevant: English-language posting channel used by MK institutions and by training providers (ABIT posts event content on LinkedIn). Captures roles that never reach MK job boards, and shows team-growth signals via employee-count and role titles. Titles like 'Regulatory Reporting Officer', 'AML Analyst', 'PSD2/SCA project' are the leading indicator this cell exists to catch.

source_name: IT.mk — tech/fintech portal (regulatory commentary)
why_relevant: Covers draft financial legislation from the technology-vendor angle (e.g. an analysis of the draft Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems: 'нови можности, но и нови предизвици'). Vendor-facing commentary and event coverage indicate when the implementation market mobilises.

source_name: MK business press cluster for event/award/hiring signals (Faktor, Makfax, Biznisvesti, Pari, eMagazin, MIA, MKD)
why_relevant: These outlets carry the announcements that first reveal conferences, licences, training academies and awards (EACHA conference hosting, KIBS instant-payments licence, MicroBalkans, Global Finance awards, ABIT enrolment). They are the discovery layer that points to the primary organiser sites which are then crawled directly.

source_name: EACHA — European Automated Clearing House Association (annual conference programme)
why_relevant: Hosted its annual conference in Skopje with ~200 delegates from 30 countries, organised by KIBS. The conference programme names the European payment-infrastructure workstreams (SEPA, instant, ISO 20022) that MK institutions are being aligned to — an agenda-level early indicator for MK payment mandates.

source_name: NBRM — Извештај за поплаките примени во банките и штедилниците (annual bank/savings-house complaints report)
why_relevant: The single most concentrated dataset on how consumers actually experience banking/payment rules in MK: annual aggregate of complaints received by banks and savings houses, by product and complaint type. Complaint spikes are the leading indicator of the provisions the regulator will revise next.

source_name: NBRM — Информации за потрошувачите (consumer information hub)
why_relevant: Landing hub that aggregates NBRM consumer-facing outputs: complaint procedure against banks, consumer rights notices, analyses, and links to the complaints reports. Best single entry point for snowballing enforcement/grievance material at the central bank.

source_name: NBRM — Дирекција за заштита на потрошувачите и финансиска едукација (ЗПФЕ)
why_relevant: Names the organisational unit that handles consumer complaints and financial education at the central bank — the actor whose outputs (procedures, mandate, contacts) define the formal grievance channel and who typically authors the complaints reports.

source_name: NBRM — Финансиска едукација (financial education programme)
why_relevant: Financial-education campaign material reveals which consumer harms the regulator considers current (fees, over-indebtedness, digital-payment fraud) — an early, softer signal that usually precedes rule changes or supervisory pressure.
